correctness.rationale: A square cannot use a letter appearing once in its ambient arc. This gives ordinary squarefreeness by deleting the middle letter and inducting. In the doubled word, a square using the largest letter must use the two listed copies at separation exactly |Z_m|, so it is the whole doubled word; one avoiding that letter must occur in the central doubled Z_{m-1}, since the outer blocks are squarefree. In a circle restricted to one traversal, the largest letter cannot appear twice; the remaining arc is exactly doubled Z_{n-1}. Translating starts gives N_n-(2^k-1). The next symbol is k+1 rather than the first symbol 1; any longer periodic factor would extend its square prefix, so none has exponent >2. For a seam-crossing square of half-length L, exactly the cuts in [L,N_n-L] retain it, including both endpoints. Those intervals are nested, and differ in size by 2^{k+1}; the last interval contains two cuts. The rank-one word and the empty starting-cut class are handled separately. A separate bit-parallel test checked all starts and allowed periods, their extensions, and all cuts through n=13, reproducing the entire histogram.
residual_risks: One traversal only. Finite enumeration corroborates the proof, not a claim for arbitrarily long factors of the periodic continuation.

evidence: A square in a doubled Zimin word is potentially equivalent to a circular square of its undoubled word, except the full doubled square is too long and offsets must be interpreted modulo the length. Cummings–Mays gives the undoubled square-free statement, not this doubled inventory.
The indexed circular-palindrome finding gives one seam palindrome at each even length, not a square test.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equal halves and reversal are distinct conditions: at rank 3 the seam palindrome of length 4 is 2112, which is not a square. The palindrome formula does not exclude nonpalindromic squares or count surviving squares after a cut.

checked_sources: Cummings–Mays §2 and arXiv:1708.00639 p.1 for context
value.rationale: Finite Zimin words are a canonical recursively defined squarefree family. Closing the seam changes what repetitions occur, and the complete inventory quantifies that change precisely; the cut distribution further tells which linear conjugates are squarefree or have any given square count. This is exact data for arbitrary rank rather than a single rank check, a restatement of squarefreeness, or an extremal bound.
residual_risks: No claim about approximate squares, arbitrary families, or exponents when more than one traversal is allowed.
